books.blurb: How AI agents get a badge, not your keys.
gist: Give each AI helper its own badge. It gets limited access and keys that run out, instead of your password.

books.title: Agent Swarms
books.blurb: When a team of AI agents works while you're away.
gist: One lead, many helpers. A lead AI splits a big job into pieces, helper AIs work on the pieces at the same time, and a checker puts the results together.
More helpers only help some jobs. Extra helpers speed up work that splits into parts, not work that needs one big idea.
You still own the result. More helpers mean more computing power and more checking. Whatever they produce, you are still responsible for it.

books.title: AI Bottlenecks
books.blurb: Why AI growth depends on power, memory and plumbing.
gist: A chip is not enough. AI chips only work with power, cooling, memory and fast links between chips, all inside a data center.
Power is the slow part. Chips can arrive in months, but getting power to a data center can take years.
Plan for the plug. The winners plan for the electricity and cooling, not just the chip.

books.title: Stablecoins & the Rails Underneath
books.blurb: How money could move on one shared record.
gist: Many records, one shared list. Banks and brokers each keep their own record of who owns what. A shared ledger keeps them in sync.
A stablecoin is a digital dollar. It can move any day, at any hour.

books.title: The Debt Loop
books.blurb: Why borrowing to pay interest feeds itself.
gist: Borrowing to pay interest. The US owes about $40 trillion and now pays over $1 trillion a year in interest, much of it paid by borrowing more.
The pipes matter. Every new IOU passes through money plumbing: bank reserves, short-term lending and money funds. Tight pipes make borrowing cost more.
Borrowed bets are fragile. Bets on Treasuries made with borrowed money work until lenders ask for cash back. New money also reaches asset owners before wage earners.

books.title: Two Schools of Economics
books.blurb: One recession, two readings of what went wrong.
gist: Keynesians fix the slump. When spending falls, government or the central bank steps in to lift it, and cools things when they overheat.
Austrians question the boom. Cheap credit pushes firms to build things people won't end up wanting, and the bust is the cleanup.
They split on money. Keynesians see the central bank as a tool to steady the economy. Austrians say its money creation sends false signals.

books.title: Stablecoin Economics
books.blurb: How stablecoin issuers and apps share the interest.
gist: A dollar with a business behind it. A stablecoin is a token meant to stay worth $1. The issuer holds the dollars in cash and short-term US government IOUs, which earn interest.
The interest gets shared. Circle says about 59 cents of each revenue dollar goes to partners such as Coinbase and Binance, plus costs. Coin holders don't get that interest.
Spending is catching up. Stablecoin payments grew 45% on last year while the number of coins barely moved (Allium). Cards still handle checkout; the change is mostly between companies.
gist_lead: A dollar with a business behind it.

books.title: The AI Ladder
books.blurb: Start low, climb only when you need to.
gist: Start on the lowest step. AI use has six steps, numbered 0 to 5. The lowest step that gets the job done is the cheapest and fastest.
Steps 0 to 2: ask, save, connect. Type a question, save a prompt you repeat, let the AI read your files and tools. For most product-manager work, step 2 is enough.
Steps 3 to 5: it runs without you. Build a small app, link steps into a workflow, or own real software. One team rebuilt a $550-700 a month tool for about $110.
gist_lead: Steps 3 to 5: it runs without you.

recap: AI use has six steps, 0 to 5: start on the lowest one that works and climb only when it stops working.
Steps 0 to 2 are asking, saving a prompt you repeat, and letting the AI use your files and tools; for most product-manager work, step 2 is enough.
Steps 3 to 5 make things that run on their own, from small apps to real software you own, so they need guardrails like limited permissions and a person's sign-off.
